puzzles.title: \text{Prove: } \sum_{i=0}^{n} F(i) = F(n+2) - 1 \text{ for the Fibonacci numbers}
puzzles.statement: \text{With } F(0) = 0,\ F(1) = 1 \text{ and } F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) \text{ for } n \ge 2 \text{, show } \sum_{i=0}^{n} F(i) = F(n+2) - 1 \text{ for all } n \ge 0.

blocks.latex: \textbf{Inductive step: } \text{assume } \sum_{i=0}^{k} F(i) = F(k+2) - 1 \text{ for some } k \ge 0.
= F(k+3) - 1 \text{ by the recurrence, since } k + 3 \ge 2.

puzzles.title: \text{Prove: Towers of Hanoi with } n \text{ disks requires } 2^n - 1 \text{ moves}

blocks.latex: \text{Let } T(n) \text{ be the minimum number of moves} \text{ to solve Towers of Hanoi with } n \text{ disks.}
\text{With 1 disk, we simply move it} \text{ from source to destination in 1 move.}
\text{Step 1: Move top } n-1 \text{ disks to auxiliary peg: } T(n-1) \text{ moves}
\text{Step 2: Move the largest disk to destination:} \text{ } 1 \text{ move}
\text{Step 3: Move } n-1 \text{ disks from auxiliary to destination: } T(n-1) \text{ moves}
\text{This method uses } T(n-1) + 1 + T(n-1) \text{ moves, so } T(n) \le 2T(n-1) + 1.

\text{Conversely, any solution must move the largest disk at least once. Before its first move the other } n-1 \text{ disks must all be on the third peg (at least } T(n-1) \text{ moves), and after its last move they must all be moved back on top of it (at least } T(n-1) \text{ more).}
\text{So } T(n) {{op:\geq}} 2T(n-1) + 1 \text{, and together with the method above, } T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1.
\text{Therefore, by strong induction, } T(n) = 2^n - 1 \text{ for all } n \ge 1.

puzzles.title: \text{Prove: binary search's recurrence } T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 \text{ is } O(\log n)
puzzles.displayTitle: Prove: T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 is O(log n)
puzzles.statement: T(1) = 1 \text{ and } T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 \text{ for powers of two } n \ge 2 \text{. Show } T(n) = O(\log_2 n).

blocks.latex: \text{Claim: } T(n) = \log_2 n + 1 \text{ for every power of two } n \ge 1 \text{. We prove it by induction on } n.
\textbf{Inductive step: } \text{assume } T(n/2) = \log_2 \tfrac{n}{2} + 1 \text{ for a power of two } n \ge 2.
T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 \text{ (one comparison, then half the array)} = \left(\log_2 \tfrac{n}{2} + 1\right) + 1
= (\log_2 n - 1) + 2 = \log_2 n + 1 \text{, which completes the induction.}
\text{For } n {{op:\geq}} 2 \text{ we have } 1 \le \log_2 n \text{, so } T(n) = \log_2 n + 1 {{op:\leq}} 2 \log_2 n.
